analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only, so no code, protocol, or authorization behavior changes in this PR.

1. docs/reference/configuration.md adds one row at head line 329 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES. It is a default-on estimator-correction switch that only changes provider-side deadline-admission arithmetic (per-batch decode charging, anchored isolated-prefill rate, newest-observation freshness). It is forwarded to the launchd provider job, which is a non-secret boolean env passthrough. It does not touch keys, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053), the cache (T-041), or the coordinator trust boundary. The disable spellings are documented. The security impact is availability or scheduling only. Because the default charges decode once per batch step, admission may accept more deadline-bound requests, which affects latency, not confidentiality or integrity. The code behind this row is not in the supplied evidence, so the claim that the documentation matches the implementation is unverified.

2. docs/reference/prediction-decision-telemetry.md adds an explanatory paragraph (head lines 30-39) and bumps the date. It states that the wire fields are unchanged. The telemetry fields carry no prompt text or token IDs, consistent with the existing statement at lines 87-88 and with T-058.

3. docs/reference/protocol-messages.md redefines sample_age_ms as time since the newest observation (patch lines 575-584). It keeps the wire schema unchanged and describes a Swift producer change in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift, which was not supplied.

Open question for integration: the behavioral claims (freshness semantics, MTP decode capping) cannot be verified from these documentation-only units. No finding is raised because no concrete regression is evidenced.
